# Layout revision report — Riverside Park Plaza (60m x 40m, outdoor)

> This is a planning draft produced by an AI agent from simulation output. It is not a permit, fire-code or crowd-safety certification; a qualified reviewer must confirm it against the venue's actual conditions and applicable regulations.

## Summary

## Before / after

Identical conditions for every iteration: scenario `entry`, 200 agents, 300 s, seed 42, density grid 2 m (fingerprint `b2047e92`). Target: max density ≤ 2 p/m² with no validation errors.

| Metric | Baseline (iteration 0) | Final (iteration 1) | Change |
|---|---|---|---|
| Max density | 2.96 p/m² | 1.97 p/m² | −0.99 p/m² (−33.4%) |
| p90 travel time | 144.5 s | 119.4 s | −25.1 s (−17.4%) |
| Mean travel time | 98.5 s | 88.5 s | −10 s (−10.2%) |
| Completed fraction | 100% | 100% | ±0 pt |
| Hotspots | 1 | 0 | −1 |
| Validation errors | 0 | 0 | ±0 |

Stop reason: **target met** — max density 1.973 ≤ target 2 p/m² with no validation errors.

## Design brief (initial constraints)

Outdoor site: crowds spread less evenly than indoors and service access matters, so aisles are wider and every gate keeps a deeper clearance. K1 sells tickets, so it sits beside G-main, out of the walking line. Food trucks will draw queues; their placement is left to the solver and checked against the simulation before anything is moved. The fire lane is unbuildable and must stay continuous; the engine enforces it.

- min_aisle_width 3 → 3.5 m
- door_clearance 5 → 6 m
- K1 pinned at (23, 6.5) beside G-main

Booth coordinates were then computed by the layout solver under these constraints.

## What changed and why

**Revision after iteration 0 → 1.** High-attraction booth F5 sits in the entrance inflow; requiring popular booths to keep a distance from entrances separates arriving visitors from booth crowds.

- popular_door_distance 0 → 12 m

## Iteration history

| Iteration | Max density (p/m²) | p90 travel (s) | Completed | Errors | Comparable |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | 2.96 | 144.5 | 100% | 0 | yes |
| 1 | 1.97 | 119.4 | 100% | 0 | yes |

## Assumptions

- Pedestrian metrics come from the **mock engine** (synthetic density field for demo purposes, not a pedestrian simulation); one scenario and seed per run, so results are a single sample, not a distribution.
- Booth popularity values are planning estimates of relative attraction, taken as given.
- Densities are peak values per grid cell over the run; hotspot thresholds are the engine's. Travel times count finished agents only.
- Geometric checks cover booth/obstacle/door-clearance/aisle rules only; egress capacity, fire code and accessibility were not assessed.
- Analysis and revision proposals by `stub`; all metrics and coordinates in this report are computed by tools.

## Unconfirmed items

- Ground slope and drainage not shown on site plan (from floor plan)
- Power hookup locations for food trucks unconfirmed (from floor plan)
- Rain contingency (tent weights / wind limits) not specified (from floor plan)
- Results not yet re-run on the real engine (OR-Tools layout, Shapely validation, JuPedSim)

---

# Layout revision report — Riverside Park Plaza (60m x 40m, outdoor)

> This is a planning draft produced by an AI agent from simulation output. It is not a permit, fire-code or crowd-safety certification; a qualified reviewer must confirm it against the venue's actual conditions and applicable regulations.

## Summary

Design brief: Outdoor site: crowds spread less evenly than indoors and service access matters, so aisles are wider and every gate keeps a deeper clearance. K1 sells tickets, so it sits beside G-main, out of the walking line. Food trucks will draw queues; their placement is left to the solver and checked against the simulation before anything is moved. The fire lane is unbuildable and must stay continuous; the engine enforces it. The solver placed the booths of Riverside Park Plaza (60m x 40m, outdoor) under those constraints and the layout was simulated under one fixed scenario. The worst congestion is hotspot #0. High-attraction booth F5 draws visitors into this zone.

Across 1 revision it kept the layout as stable as possible and changed only what the simulation pointed at: High-attraction booth F5 sits in the entrance inflow; requiring popular booths to keep a distance from entrances separates arriving visitors from booth crowds. Each revised layout was re-validated and re-simulated with the identical scenario, so the before/after comparison below reflects layout changes only.
